Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Dynamics Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge Dynamics' Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; and Casey Wong, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge Dynamics' performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI Pro and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: delivering a strong Rule of 40 score, maintaining robust NRR performance, improving our LTV/CAC ratio, analyzing and mitigating churn, updating our full-year revenue guidance, and accelerating expansion revenue from existing customers.

These efforts have positioned us for sustained growth in the AI-native cloud management space. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 78%, and operating income was $33 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $610 to $615 million.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our financial highlights, I want to focus on one of the key metrics that best captures the health and momentum of our SaaS business here at CloudForge Dynamics: our Rule of 40 score. For those new to our calls, the Rule of 40 is the simple yet powerful sum of our year-over-year revenue growth rate and our free cash flow margin percentage. It's a north star for SaaS investors, balancing top-line acceleration with bottom-line discipline—much like how Snowflake has used it to signal sustainable hypergrowth or ServiceNow has leveraged it through margin expansion in their workflow automation platform.

In Q3 FY2024, we delivered a Rule of 40 score of 43%, up from 38% in the prior-year quarter and 41% in Q2 of this year. This marks our eighth straight quarter above 40%, underscoring the operating leverage we're unlocking as we scale our AI-native cloud management platform. Let me break it down: Revenue growth was 28% YoY to $152 million in quarterly revenue. This was driven by a healthy mix of 22% expansion from existing customers—our dollar-based net retention rate, or NRR, held steady at 118%, fueled by land-and-expand motions in our multi-tenant Analytics Engine—and 6% from 145 net new logos, including several seven-figure deals with Fortune 500 enterprises in financial services and healthcare. Excluding the impact of our recent acquisition of OptiScale, which added about 2 points to growth, organic growth was a robust 26%.

Free cash flow margin was at 15%, or $23 million in free cash flow, representing 320 basis points of expansion year-over-year. We've now achieved positive FCF margins for 11 consecutive quarters, ahead of peers like Datadog, which is still navigating FCF volatility amid heavy R&D investments. Key drivers include our non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 22%, thanks to sales and marketing efficiency—our CAC payback period shortened to 14 months from 17—and G&A leverage as headcount growth slowed to just 8% quarter-over-quarter.

Zooming out to the trailing 12 months, our Rule of 40 stands at 45%, with revenue growth of 31% and FCF margin of 14%. This puts us in elite company within the SaaS universe, comparable to high performers like Monday.com during their pivot to enterprise or HubSpot's post-IPO maturation phase.

Geographically, North America remains our powerhouse at 72% of revenue, growing 25% YoY on deep penetration into hyperscalers like AWS and Azure—our integrations with Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Fabric have driven 35% uptake in AI workload optimization modules. EMEA accelerated to 42% growth, now 18% of total revenue, propelled by GDPR-compliant data sovereignty features that won us deals with European banks akin to those served by Crowdstrike in cybersecurity. APAC, at 10% of revenue, surged 55% on our Tokyo data center launch and partnerships with SoftBank, though forex headwinds shaved 2 points off reported growth. Emerging markets like LATAM contributed 5% growth but remain a focus for FY2025 ramp.

Under the hood, our Q3 launch of ForgeAI Pro—a generative AI layer for predictive cost optimization and anomaly detection—has been a game-changer, contributing 12% to new ACV bookings. We've seen seat expansion rates hit 2.5x in early adopters, mirroring the virality Snowflake experienced with Snowpark for ML workloads. On the efficiency front, we've migrated 85% of our infrastructure to our own Kubernetes-orchestrated edge platform, reducing hosting costs by 18% YoY and boosting gross margins to 78%. R&D investments, at 22% of revenue, are yielding a 3x ROI on AI patents filed this year, positioning us ahead of the curve as enterprises grapple with 30-50% cloud spend overruns amid the GenAI boom.

Looking ahead, we're laser-focused on Rule of 40 expansion through three levers: product-led growth, targeting 125% NRR by EOY via unbundled AI add-ons; go-to-market optimization, with a 20% increase in our mid-market inside sales team to capture the $10B TAM underserved by legacy players like VMware; and margin discipline, guiding for 18-20% FCF margins in FY2025 as we lap higher comps and realize $15M in annualized synergies from OptiScale.

For the full year, we’re raising revenue guidance to $610-615 million, or 30-31% growth, and FCF to $85-90 million at a 14% margin, implying a year-end Rule of 40 north of 45%. This trajectory reflects not just cyclical tailwinds from digital transformation—think the $500B+ public cloud spend forecasted by Gartner—but our durable moat in agentic AI for SaaS ops.

Turning now to our net revenue retention—or NRR—which remains a cornerstone of our SaaS flywheel and a testament to the stickiness of our AI-powered DevOps platform. For Q3, we delivered an NRR of 118%, marking our eighth consecutive quarter above 110% and accelerating 3 points sequentially from 115% in Q2. This performance underscores the strength of our land-and-expand model, where customers start with our core CI/CD pipelines—think GitLab Ultimate-style workflows enhanced with our proprietary ML ops layer—and scale into higher-value modules like predictive deployment analytics and autonomous security scanning.

To break it down by drivers, our starting ARR cohort for the quarter was around $450 million from customers active at the beginning of Q3. Expansion was the standout at 16.2%, up 200 basis points quarter-over-quarter. This was fueled by two key initiatives: first, the launch of our ForgeAI Optimizer module, which uses generative AI—integrated with models like Anthropic's Claude and AWS Bedrock—to automate resource provisioning and cut cloud costs by up to 30% for customers. We saw 42% adoption among our top 500 logos, driving an average ACV uplift of $145K per expansion deal. Second, our usage-based pricing tier for high-volume workloads, similar to Snowflake's consumption model, kicked in meaningfully; variable revenue from this grew 28% QoQ as enterprises like our new wins in fintech—echoing the scale of Stripe or Plaid customers—ramped workloads amid AI training surges. Notably, net expansion in our Enterprise segment hit 22%, reflecting multi-year contracts with auto-renewal clauses locking in 95%+ renewal rates.

Contraction remained contained at just 1.8% of starting ARR, flat sequentially and well below our historical average of 2.5%. We attribute this to proactive customer success interventions via our HealthScore dashboard, which flags at-risk accounts 45 days early using churn prediction algorithms trained on 5+ years of telemetry data. Downgrades were minimal, primarily in mid-market SMBs optimizing post-optimization amid softer macro conditions, but offset by our bundling of premium support SKUs.

Churn—both logo and revenue—was de minimis at 3.1%, down 50 bps QoQ. Revenue churn specifically was 2.7%, driven by just 14 logo losses out of 1,200+ customers, mostly non-strategic SMBs under $50K ACV that didn't expand beyond core pipelines. Our dollar-based churn stayed under 4%, aligning with peers like Datadog or New Relic, and we saw zero churn in our top 100 customers, where median tenure now exceeds 4 years.

Regionally, this NRR strength was broad-based. North America contributed 112%—our core market, bolstered by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure—while EMEA expanded to 122%, thanks to GDPR-compliant AI features resonating with telcos and banks like those using PagerDuty at scale. APAC lagged slightly at 108%, pressured by yen weakness and delayed RFPs in Japan, but we're countering this with localized sovereign cloud integrations and a Tokyo-based sales pod, targeting 115%+ in Q4.

Strategically, these dynamics validate our platformization bet: by embedding AI-native capabilities akin to Harness or CircleCI's evolutions, we're not just retaining but growing ARR per customer by 24% YoY. Looking forward, we expect NRR to stabilize at 117-120% in Q4 as seasonal renewals ramp, with upside from our upcoming ForgeAI Guardrails for compliance automation—already in beta with 15 early adopters. This positions us to outpace the SaaS index average of ~105-110%, even in a high-interest-rate environment where capex scrutiny favors proven ROI platforms like ours.

Moving to our core efficiency metrics, I'd like to dive into our Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio, or LTV/CAC, which remains a cornerstone of our SaaS flywheel here at CloudForge. We're the leading AI-powered collaboration platform, blending workflow automation akin to Asana with real-time comms like Slack, all integrated natively with hyperscalers like AWS and Microsoft Azure. Our LTV/CAC ratio for Q3 ended at 4.2x, up from 3.8x in Q2 and a robust improvement over the 3.1x we reported this time last year. This puts us firmly in the elite tier of SaaS peers—think companies like Snowflake or HubSpot, where ratios north of 4x signal scalable unit economics and predictable free cash flow generation.

To give you the full picture, our LTV is calculated as ARPU times gross margin times average customer lifetime. Q3 ARPU came in at $48,000 on an ARR basis, reflecting strong expansion in our enterprise tier, where median ACV now exceeds $150K thanks to upsells like our new AI Agent Builder module. Gross margins held steady at 82%, benefiting from our 95%+ infrastructure efficiency on AWS Graviton instances, which shaved another 200 basis points off COGS YoY. Average customer lifetime expanded to 52 months, or about 4.3 years, driven by our league-leading NRR of 118%—we're not just retaining; we're expanding 18% annually within cohort.

On the CAC side, it clocked in at $11,400 per new customer, down 8% QoQ. This is sales and marketing spend—$145 million in the quarter—divided by our 12,700 net new logos. The efficiency gains stem from our accelerated product-led growth motion: 62% of new Annual Contract Value now comes from self-serve signups via our freemium funnel, up from 48% a year ago. We've refined our viral coefficient to 1.35 through in-app referral loops and Slack-like workspace sharing, mimicking Dropbox's early playbook but supercharged with GenAI personalization. Paid CAC for SMBs dropped to $2.8K via Google Performance Max campaigns optimized for LTV signals, while enterprise CAC held at $45K but with payback periods compressing to 14 months from 18.

Trend-wise, this 4.2x ratio marks our fifth straight quarter of expansion, outpacing the Bessemer Cloud Index average of 3.5x amid the macro squeeze on ad spend. YoY, LTV grew 28% while CAC fell 12%, fueled by three key initiatives: technical stack modernization with serverless event streaming using Kafka on Confluent Cloud, reducing onboarding friction by 40% and boosting Day 1 activation from 65% to 88%, mirroring Atlassian's Jira evolution and slashing low-quality leads; AI-driven personalization via our ForgeAI engine, which predicts churn with 92% accuracy, enabling proactive upsells that added $22M in expansion ARR with 15% LTV uplift for AI-engaged cohorts; and partner ecosystem leverage, with co-sell motions via AWS Marketplace and Microsoft AppSource driving 25% of enterprise wins and blended CAC payback under 12 months, akin to Zoom's Teams integrations.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse at 4.8x LTV/CAC, anchored by Fortune 500 logos like a major Big Four consultancy expanding to 50K seats. EMEA surged to 4.0x, up 35% YoY, on GDPR-compliant data sovereignty features and wins in DACH via SAP partnerships. APAC lags at 3.2x due to longer sales cycles and forex headwinds, but our Singapore hub launch and localization into Japanese/Chinese have stabilized churn at 1.2% monthly, with Q4 guidance pointing to 3.8x parity.

Strategically, this metric underscores our trajectory toward higher margins and positions us for 25-30% FCF margins by FY25. We're guiding LTV/CAC to 4.5x+ in Q4 as PLG scales to 70% of intake and AI expansions accelerate NRR toward 122%. Risks like macro-driven SMB caution could pressure ARPU, but our 70% gross dollar retention buffers that. Compared to peers, we're ahead of ServiceNow's 3.9x but trailing Datadog's 5.1x—we're closing the gap via margin discipline. In short, our LTV/CAC isn't just healthy; it's compounding our moat in a $200B+ collaboration TAM.

I'll now turn to our churn analysis, which continues to be a cornerstone of our financial health here at CloudForge Dynamics, where we deliver our flagship SaaS platform for enterprise collaboration and workflow automation—think of us as the connective tissue between tools like Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, and Jira for mid-market and enterprise teams. In Q3, we maintained strong retention metrics amid a challenging macro environment, with gross dollar retention at 92%—flat quarter-over-quarter but up 200 basis points year-over-year—and NRR expanding to 118%, driven by 18% net expansion in our top 20% of customers. Logo churn was 4.2% annualized, primarily in the SMB segment under $100K ARR, while enterprise accounts above $1M ARR saw near-zero contraction.

We track churn rigorously through cohort analysis and RFM segmentation, and here are the primary drivers along with our mitigation strategies. First, macroeconomic pressures and budget scrutiny accounted for 45% of churn attribution. Ongoing economic uncertainty, with slower GDP growth, led to cost optimization, especially among SMBs representing 60% of logo churn, who cited budget reallocation in 70% of exit surveys—echoing industry trends like those at HubSpot. Customers in professional services and retail trimmed SaaS stacks to consolidate around big tech incumbents like Microsoft 365.

Second, product and integration friction made up 30%, with 25% of churn from integration gaps, particularly with emerging AI workflows. For instance, delays in native Copilot integration affected 12% of departures, compared to faster rollouts by Monday.com. Uptime at 99.95%—below our 99.99% SLA—hit EMEA harder due to GDPR issues, contributing to regional GDR of 89% versus 94% in North America.

Third, onboarding and usage gaps were 15%, with post-pricing reset cohorts showing 22% lower Day-30 active user rates and 3x higher churn risk, acute in APAC where localization lags led to 6.5% logo churn.

Fourth, competitive displacement was 10%, with rivals like Asana Enterprise and ClickUp eroding mid-market contracts via freemium funnels, plus super app consolidation to Notion or Coda.

Regionally, North America drove 55% of ARR but only 40% of churn, EMEA saw 5.1% annualized due to regulations, and APAC held at 4.8% with expansion pressure from currency.

We're investing $25M in FY24 retention initiatives, targeting 95% GDR and 112% NRR by year-end, in line with top peers like Snowflake and Datadog. Key strategies include our AI-powered churn prediction engine, trained on 5+ years of data, achieving 87% precision at 90 days out, reducing high-risk churn by 22% and recovering $4.2M ARR via automated playbooks. We've doubled our CSM-to-ARR ratio to 1:15M with Enterprise pods, boosting expansion 35% and shortening onboarding 40% to lift Day-30 adoption to 78%. Product prioritization accelerates Copilot beta to GA in Q4 and GDPR zones in August, plus our SaaS Stack Optimizer AI tool. Pricing innovations like usage-based for SMBs cut churn 14% in tests, and regional tailoring includes APAC embeds with LINE/WeChat and EMEA zero-trust certs.

Strategically, 65% of NRR comes from cross-sells, and we'll verticalize like with healthcare HIPAA modules. Overall, these efforts position us for Rule of 40 expansion to 55% in FY25.

Now, let's dive into expansion revenue from existing customers, one of our most critical growth drivers. In the SaaS world, sustainable growth means turning initial footholds into multi-year juggernauts. For Q3, expansion revenue hit approximately $33 million, representing 22% of our total revenue—a 12-point year-over-year mix increase. This outpaced overall growth, with our dollar-based net expansion rate at 118% for customers with at least $10K ARR last year, improving sequentially and marking 10 straight quarters above 110%, in line with Snowflake and Datadog. About 62% came from upsells/cross-sells, 25% from seat expansions, and the rest from pricing.

Multi-product adoption is key: over 65% of top 500 customers—generating 75% ARR—use three+ modules, up from 48% YoY. Our CI/CD beachhead leads to ForgeAI Test, driving significant bookings with 3x attach rates, delivering 40-50% faster cycles like GitHub Copilot. Consumption pricing on workloads grew usage 65% YoY, with fintech scaling adding substantial ARR.

North America was 72% of expansion at 42% YoY, EMEA 62% to 18% mix via GDPR add-ons, APAC 105% off small base with Kubernetes integrations. Cohorts like Q3 2023 hit 135% DBNER at 12 months. We've doubled CSMs, added QBRs tying to ROI, with sub-1% gross dollar churn.

For H2/FY25, deeper AI integrations with Anthropic/Hugging Face, vertical packs like Retail DevOps, and channel co-sells via AWS/Azure target sustained momentum. With a growing ARR base 85% multi-year, we're set for 30%+ organic growth.

Finally, on full-year revenue guidance, building on Q3's strength at $152 million and 28% growth, beating prior expectations. Subscription revenue, 94% of total, grew robustly from core DevOps and AI Observability, with AutoScale AI contributing to expansions. We're raising FY24 outlook to $610-615 million, implying 30-31% growth, up from prior, with subscription at ~$575 million.

Customer metrics: ending with 5,000+ customers, 650 over $100K ACV up 35%. Land-and-expand shines with 98% cohort retention. Sales productivity high, 65% multi-year bookings.

Regionally: Americas 72% at 44% growth via hyperscalers; EMEA 18% at 48% with GDPR AI; APAC 8% at 35% via sovereign cloud; LatAm 60% off small base. Secular tailwinds in AI/multi-cloud drive 2x faster cycles. Q4 platform adds federated learning, dynamic pricing lifts averages 8%. Conservatism for SMBs baked in, FCF at 14%, op margins 22%. Q4 guide $160-165 million.

This positions us strongly in the $100B+ market. Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, like ForgeAI Pro, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including 85% migration to Kubernetes edge and federated learning for privacy.

And now Casey will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Casey Wong:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Guardrails. This new feature significantly improves compliance automation and predictive security. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy of embedding AI-native tools for land-and-expand.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI Pro on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI Pro has had a transformative impact on our growth, contributing 12% to new ACV bookings and driving 22% of expansions this quarter. Attach rates are at 42% among eligible customers, with 2.5x seat growth in early adopters—well above our initial expectations, which targeted 30% adoption. This has accelerated sales cycles by 25% in enterprise deals and boosted NRR by 3 points, exceeding forecasts as customers realize 30% cost savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Lisa. International expansion is a top priority, with APAC surging 55% this quarter to 10% of revenue. We've launched our Tokyo data center and partnered with SoftBank, countering forex with localized integrations. Key targets include Japan for sovereign cloud RFPs, Singapore/Australia for fintech, and broader emerging markets like LatAm at 60% growth. EMEA hit 42% on GDPR features. We plan 20% sales ramp in APAC for FY25, aiming for 15% of revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Mike. Churn is tightly managed at 3.1% revenue this quarter, with GDR at 92% amid macro pressures like budget scrutiny (45% of cases) and integration friction. Logo churn at 4.2% annualized, mostly SMBs. NRR trended up to 118%, with 16.2% expansion offsetting low contraction/churn. Strategies include AI prediction at 87% accuracy recovering $4.2M ARR, doubled CSMs boosting adoption 78%, roadmap accelerations like Copilot/GDPR, usage pricing cutting SMB churn 14%, and regional tailoring. Expect NRR 117-120% Q4, GDR to 95%.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Rule of 40: Report the Rule of 40 metric (Revenue Growth + Profit Margin).
NRR performance: Report NRR and explain drivers (expansion, contraction, churn).
LTV/CAC ratio: Report the Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio.
Churn analysis: Discuss reasons for customer churn and mitigation strategies.
Full-year revenue guidance: Provide revenue guidance for the full fiscal year.
Expansion revenue: Detail revenue growth from existing customers.

aspect_summary.Rule of 40: Q3 FY2024 Rule of 40 score of 43% (28% YoY revenue growth + 15% FCF margin), up from 38% prior year and 41% Q2; TTM 45%; FY24 year-end >45%.
aspect_summary.NRR performance: Q3 NRR 118% (up 3pts QoQ), driven by 16.2% expansion (ForgeAI Optimizer adoption, usage-based pricing), 1.8% contraction, and 3.1% churn (revenue churn 2.7%).

aspect_summary.Full-year revenue guidance: FY24 revenue guidance raised to $610-615 million (30-31% YoY growth).
